messages:
oliver: hey team, i'm Oliver — started today. trying to run the infra pipeline from my fork and hit a "failed to pull image" 403 from GHCR. anyone seen this during onboarding?

maya: welcome Oliver! :wave: yes — common onboarding gotcha. can you paste the exact error from the Buildkite agent?

oliver: here's the log excerpt:
```
Step: pull image
failed to pull image \"ghcr.io/redwood/ci-runner:latest\": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to resolve reference \"ghcr.io/redwood/ci-runner:latest\": denied: requested access to the resource is denied
{"message":"You must have read access to the container registry."}
```

ben: forks don't get the org GitHub App token by default and our GH Actions/pipeline secrets are blocked for forked PRs. two things to check: 1) did you accept the GitHub App install invite? 2) are you in the redwood-ci Okta group for Buildkite pipeline permissions?

oliver: i accepted the org invite but didn't see an app invite email. Okta shows me in the company directory but not in redwood-ci yet.

oncall-bot: Access request created: CI-14567 owner=maya status=pending reviewers=[infra-oncall].

maya: adding you to redwood-ci now. FYI there's sometimes a short SCIM delay. if the app invite isn't present you can either: a) install the app on your fork (if org policy allows), b) ask a maintainer to run CI in the upstream repo, or c) get a scoped PAT packages:read (short-lived) injected as a masked CI_GHCR_TOKEN.

oliver: prefer to avoid maintainer-run loops. can i get a short-lived token for now? what scope exactly?

ben: create PAT with only packages:read and repo:public_repo if you need to push test branches. we create a short 12h token for new hires. maya, can you provision?

maya: done — added masked pipeline var CI_GHCR_TOKEN to Oliver's Buildkite pipeline and added him to redwood-ci. infra-bot created the ticket for tracking.

oncall-bot: Ticket CI-14567 updated: token added, Okta sync requested.

oliver: restarted the build after token was added and now the agent pulls the image and proceeds. :tada: thanks!

ben: long-term we want to avoid manual tokens. follow-ups: add a note to onboarding about forks+GHCR, add a fallback to Docker Hub mirror for the runner image, and consider a pipeline check that runs sensitive jobs in upstream for fork PRs. filing a tiny docs PR and an RFC.

maya: +1 — i'll update the onboarding checklist with a one-liner: "Accept GitHub App install and verify redwood-ci Okta membership; if you hit GHCR 403, request a short-lived packages:read token or run CI upstream."

oliver: great — i'll open a small PR to clarify the steps I followed. really appreciate the quick help and warm welcome!
